primitives.name: Time-Variant Bradley-Terry Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: We successfully identify teams significantly stronger or weaker than the average, with stronger teams placing higher in the previous seasons' ladder and leading the activity in the Forward 50 zone, goal shots and scoring over their opponents.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P(W_i > W_j)': 'Probability that team i beats team j (dimensionless)', '\\theta_i': 'Strength parameter for team i (log-odds scale)', '\\theta_j': 'Strength parameter for team j (log-odds scale)', 'f(t_{ij})': 'Time-varying feature function capturing temporal dynamics (log-odds scale)', 't_{ij}': 'Timestamp of match between i and j (unit: match index)'}
primitives.assumptions: Teams are independent, matches are binary outcomes, and the log-odds of victory is linearly separable by team strength and time-varying features.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when \theta_i - \theta_j approaches infinity, yielding deterministic outcomes; otherwise, continuous probabilistic predictions hold.

layer2.mapping: Maps Bradley-Terry's log-odds framework to GSI's posterior predictive distribution via Bayesian updating, where team strengths become random variables calibrated against observed match outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted vs. actual match outcomes, cross-entropy loss, and calibration curve sharpness.

primitives.name: Fixed Home-Field Advantage Term
primitives.verbatim_quote: Playing at home is confirmed to create an advantage regardless of team strengths.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P(W_h)': 'Probability of winning at home (dimensionless)', 'P(W_a)': 'Probability of winning away (dimensionless)', '\\delta_H': 'Constant home-field advantage effect size (log-odds)', 'H': 'Indicator variable for home game (binary)'}
primitives.assumptions: Home advantage is constant across all teams and time periods, acting as an additive shift in the log-odds of victory.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \delta_H = 0, home advantage vanishes, reducing to a symmetric model; non-zero \delta_H introduces bias favoring the home team.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's situational state-transition logic where "home court" is a persistent environmental feature influencing transition probabilities between game states.
layer2.telemetry: Difference in win rates between home and away games, adjusted for team strength.

primitives.name: Forward 50 Zone Activity Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Complex machine learning algorithms have been developed to predict match outcomes post-game, but their lack of interpretability hampers an understanding of the factors that affect a team's performance.

primitives.assumptions: Zone occupancy is a sufficient statistic for spatial dominance, and contributions from different cells are additively separable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Saturates when all cells are occupied, representing maximum possible spatial control; zero indicates complete absence from the zone.

layer2.mapping: Embeds spatial activity counts into GSE's multi-dimensional state space, where F_{50,i} becomes a state variable driving possession transitions and scoring opportunities.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between F_{50,i} and subsequent goal-scoring events, conditional on opponent's spatial distribution.

primitives.name: Goal Shots Differential
primitives.verbatim_quote: Using data from the male competition of the Australian Football League, seasons 2015 to 2023, we estimate team strengths and the factors impacting them by fitting flexible BradleyTerry models.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Delta G_i': 'Goal shots differential for team i (dimensionless)', 'G_{i}': 'Total goal shots taken by team i (count)', 'G_{j}': 'Total goal shots taken by opposing team j (count)'}
primitives.assumptions: Goal shots are independent Bernoulli trials with team-specific success probabilities, and the difference captures offensive efficiency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Positive \Delta G_i indicates superior shooting volume or accuracy; negative values suggest defensive pressure or poor finishing.

layer2.mapping: Integrates shot differentials into GSE's tactical state graph, where \Delta G_i influences edge weights between possession states and scoring nodes.
layer2.telemetry: Brier score of predicted vs. actual goal conversion rates, stratified by \Delta G_i deciles.

primitives.name: Logistic Regression
primitives.verbatim_quote: The probability of Team i winning in round r against Team j is therefore calculated as logit(P(Yijr = 1)) = λi -λj, where we dropped the r subscript since strengths are constant throughout a season.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P(Y_{ijr}=1)': 'Probability of Team i beating Team j in round r, dimensionless', '\\lambda_i': 'Team i strength parameter, log-odds scale', '\\lambda_j': 'Team j strength parameter, log-odds scale'}
primitives.assumptions: Constant team strengths across seasons, binary outcome (win/loss), independence of observations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when |λi - λj| → ∞, causing perfect separation.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian logistic regression with uniform priors on team strengths maps exactly to maximum likelihood estimation under the Bradley-Terry framework. Conformal prediction intervals for win probabilities can be constructed via calibration.
layer2.telemetry: Observed win-loss frequencies vs. predicted probabilities; Brier score for calibration; AUC-ROC for discriminatory power.

primitives.name: Home Advantage Effect
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the AFL, the only effect that is specific to all contest pairs and constant over time is whether or not the team is designated as Home or Away.
primitives.assumptions: Binary home/away indicator captures stadium, crowd, travel effects collectively.
primitives.breakdown_regime: No singularity; bounded additive shift in logits.

layer2.mapping: Additive home advantage δ in logits corresponds to a multiplicative factor exp(δ) in odds. This is identical to including a contest-level intercept in a generalized linear model. For GSE, this becomes a state-transition bias conditioned on venue and roster composition.
layer2.telemetry: Difference in win rates between home and away games; residual analysis after accounting for team strengths.

reasoning_traces.think: This chapter window systematically compares nested specifications of the Bradley-Terry model—standard, contest-specific, and time-variant—across multiple training window lengths. The core insight is that allowing parameters to vary temporally or contextually reduces out-of-sample misclassification error, as evidenced by lower AIC values and higher test-set accuracy. However, increased flexibility risks overfitting, particularly when training on shorter windows or incorporating high-dimensional predictive information.
